question: What wage periods does section 16 of the Code on Wages list, and what is their maximum length?
expected_conditions: Daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly; no wage period may exceed one month.
original_title: The Code on Wages, 2019 (No. 29 of 2019)
source_quote:
The employer shall fix the wage period for employees either as daily or weekly or
fortnightly or monthly subject to the condition that no wage period in respect of any employee
shall be more than a month

question: According to section 17(1)(i) of the Code on Wages, when are daily-basis wages paid?
expected_conditions: At the end of the shift.
original_title: The Code on Wages, 2019 (No. 29 of 2019)
source_quote: daily basis, at the end of the shift

question: Under section 17(1)(iv) of the Code on Wages, what is the stated time limit for monthly wages?
expected_conditions: Before expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.
original_title: The Code on Wages, 2019 (No. 29 of 2019)
source_quote:
monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding
month.

question: How often does section 8(4) of the Code on Wages say minimum rates should ordinarily be reviewed or revised?
expected_conditions: Ordinarily at an interval not exceeding five years.
original_title: The Code on Wages, 2019 (No. 29 of 2019)
source_quote:
The appropriate Government shall review or revise minimum rates of wages ordinarily
at an interval not exceeding five years.

question: When proposals to fix or revise minimum wages are published under section 8(1)(b) of the Code on Wages, what is the minimum period before they are considered?
expected_conditions: The specified date must be not less than two months from notification.
original_title: The Code on Wages, 2019 (No. 29 of 2019)
source_quote:
by notification publish its proposals for the information of persons likely to
be affected thereby and specify a date not less than two months from the date of the
notification on which the proposals shall be taken into consideration.

question: At what worker count does section 4(1) of the Industrial Relations Code require grievance redressal committees?
expected_conditions: Every industrial establishment employing twenty or more workers must have one or more.
original_title: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (No. 35 of 2020)
source_quote:
Every industrial establishment employing twenty or more workers shall have
one or more Grievance Redressal Committees for resolution of disputes arising out of
individual grievances.

question: Under section 4 of the Industrial Relations Code, what is the maximum size of a grievance redressal committee and what representation requirements apply?
expected_conditions: No more than ten members; equal employer and worker representation, and adequate women-worker representation not less than their proportion in the establishment.
original_title: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (No. 35 of 2020)
source_quote:
(2) The Grievance Redressal Committee shall consist of equal number of members
representing the employer and the workers to be chosen in such manner as may be prescribed.
(3) The chairperson of the Grievance Redressal Committee shall be selected from
among persons representing the employer and the workers alternatively on rotational basis
every year.
(4) The total number of members of the Grievance Redressal Committee shall not
exceed ten:

additional_sources.source_quote:
Provided that there shall be adequate representation of women workers in the
Grievance Redressal Committee and such representation shall not be less than the proportion
of women workers to the total workers employed in the industrial establishment.

question: How often does the chairperson of a grievance redressal committee rotate under section 4(3) of the Industrial Relations Code?
expected_conditions: The chairperson alternates annually between employer and worker representatives.
original_title: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (No. 35 of 2020)
source_quote:
The chairperson of the Grievance Redressal Committee shall be selected from
among persons representing the employer and the workers alternatively on rotational basis
every year.

question: What period does section 4(6) of the Industrial Relations Code give a grievance redressal committee to complete proceedings?
expected_conditions: It may complete proceedings within thirty days of receiving the application.
original_title: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (No. 35 of 2020)
source_quote:
The Grievance Redressal Committee may complete its proceedings within thirty
days of receipt of the application under sub-section (5).

question: Under section 14(3) of the Industrial Relations Code, what support level is specified for recognition as sole negotiating union when multiple registered unions function?
expected_conditions: Fifty-one per cent or more of workers on the establishment muster roll, verified as prescribed.
original_title: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (No. 35 of 2020)
source_quote:
the Trade Union having fifty-one per cent. or more
workers on the muster roll of that industrial establishment, verified in such manner as may
be prescribed, supporting that Trade Union shall be recognised by the employer of the
industrial establishment, as the sole negotiating union of the workers.

question: How does section 2(35) of the Code on Social Security describe a gig worker?
expected_conditions: A person who performs work or participates in a work arrangement and earns from it outside a traditional employer-employee relationship.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)

question: Under section 52 of the Code on Social Security, when can an Employees’ Insurance Court order be appealed to the High Court, and within what period?
expected_conditions: An appeal lies if there is a substantial question of law and must be filed within sixty days of the order.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
An appeal shall lie to the High Court from an order of an Employees' Insurance
Court, if it involves a substantial question of law.
(3) The appeal shall be filed under this section within a period of sixty days from the
date of the order made by the Employees' Insurance Court.

question: What does the proviso to section 53(1) of the Code on Social Security say about the five-year gratuity service condition for death, disablement, or expiry of fixed-term employment?
expected_conditions: Five years of continuous service is not necessary where termination is due to death, disablement, expiration of fixed-term employment, or another event notified by the Central Government.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
Provided further that the completion of continuous service of five years shall not be
necessary where the termination of the employment of any employee is due to death or
disablement or expiration of fixed term employment or happening of any such event as
may be notified by the Central Government:

question: What gratuity rate does the Code on Social Security state for a seasonal establishment employee not employed throughout the year?
expected_conditions: Seven days’ wages for each season.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
employee who is employed in a seasonal
establishment and who is not so employed throughout the year, the employer shall pay the
gratuity at the rate of seven days' wages for each season:

question: When sufficient cause prevented a timely gratuity appeal under section 56(8) of the Code on Social Security, what additional period may be allowed?
expected_conditions: The appropriate Government or appellate authority may extend the sixty-day appeal period by a further sixty days if satisfied of sufficient cause.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from preferring
the appeal within the said period of sixty days, extend the said period by a further period of
sixty days:

question: What does the OSH Code say about the cost of the prescribed annual health examination or test?
expected_conditions: It is provided free of cost to such categories as prescribed by the appropriate Government.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)

question: Which government constitutes the National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board under section 16 of the OSH Code?
expected_conditions: The Central Government constitutes it by notification.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)
source_quote:
The Central Government shall, by notification, constitute the National
Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board (hereinafter in this Code referred to as the
National Board

question: According to section 22(1) of the OSH Code, how must worker and employer representation compare on a Safety Committee?
expected_conditions: Worker representatives must not be fewer than employer representatives.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)
source_quote:
the number of representatives of workers on the Committee
shall not be less than the number of representatives of the employer

question: What worker threshold does section 24(1)(v) of the OSH Code mention for a canteen facility?
expected_conditions: An establishment where one hundred or more workers, including contract labourers, are ordinarily employed.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)
source_quote:
facilities of canteen in an establishment for employees thereof, wherein one
hundred or more workers including contract labourers are ordinarily employed;
